sources.title: C. P. Burgess, Introduction to Effective Field Theory
sources.locator: §2.1, printed pp. 13–15, redundant-interaction argument and equations (21)–(26); §§3.1–3.3, printed pp. 28–33, effective-interaction class, power-counting rules, and effective-Lagrangian logic.

contents.name: §2.1: redundant interactions and the leading-equation field redefinition, equations (21)–(26)

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete pp. 13–15 argument, including the finite-order action expansion, the identity-leading change of variables, the integration-by-parts scalar example, and the leading-equation substitution.
source_review.supports: A leading-equation density can be canceled at one retained order by an actual field redefinition; the stated compact-support example fixes the sign convention used for the local scalar verification.
source_review.limitations: Burgess's generic statement is pedagogical source context. The batch item independently derives its Euler derivative, boundary identity, inverse to the retained order, and induced quartic term; no all-orders or quantum-observable equivalence is imported.

contents.name: §3.1: a specified class of effective interactions
contents.support: The section fixes field, coefficient, derivative, and scale conventions before using its example power count.
contents.limitations: The selected class and dimensional assumptions are source-specific; the authored contract explicitly records its own field weights, finite jet and polynomial cutoffs, and separate operator scale.

contents.name: §3.2: power-counting rules
contents.support: The source relates the chosen interaction order, graph loop order, and low-energy scale ratios under its stated EFT action class.
contents.limitations: Its graph estimates are not imported as a universal truncation error or coefficient prediction; the local contract defines a formal canonical-dimension/loop truncation only.

contents.name: §3.3: effective-Lagrangian logic
contents.support: The discussion separates an accuracy target, the order required by a model-specific power count, and the terms needed at that order.
contents.limitations: No observable accuracy target or experimental coefficient fit is adopted in this batch; the authored item does not infer a numerical error from power counting.

sources.title: David B. Kaplan, Five lectures on effective field theory
sources.locator: §1.2, printed pp. 4–7, local operators and scaling dimension in the relativistic scalar example; §§2.4.1–2.4.2, printed pp. 22–23, gauge and exact/approximate global symmetries.

contents.name: §1.2: relativistic local operators and scaling dimension
contents.support: The lecture derives the four-dimensional scalar mass dimension from the dimensionless action, writes symmetry-allowed local terms with cutoff-suppressed coefficients, and explains fixed-order selection by scaling.
contents.limitations: The scalar power count is a worked relativistic example, not the proof of the batch's finite-jet quotient or any general EFT accuracy theorem.

contents.name: §2.4.1: gauge symmetries
contents.support: The lecture explains that gauge redundancy and low-energy field choices affect how symmetry is represented in an EFT.
contents.limitations: The item uses the exact local principal-bundle and representation suppliers for its mathematical definitions; Kaplan is not substituted for their bundle or connection arguments.

contents.name: §2.4.2: exact and approximate global symmetries
contents.support: The discussion distinguishes exact symmetries from explicitly broken ones and motivates recording the chosen symmetry action on allowed operators.
contents.limitations: The example uses an exact declared symmetry only; it imports no naturalness estimate, symmetry-breaking magnitude, or phenomenological conclusion.

sources.title: Juan Carlos Criado and Manuel Pérez-Victoria, Field redefinitions in effective theories at higher orders
sources.locator: §3, printed pp. 9–10, equations (3.1)–(3.2), on the first-order equation-of-motion relation and higher-order limitation; §5.1, printed pp. 16–17, equations (5.1)–(5.3), on order-by-order local redefinitions and induced higher-order terms.

contents.name: §3: field redefinitions versus equations of motion, equations (3.1)–(3.2)
contents.support: The paper derives the first-order change of an action under a local field redefinition and warns that dropping higher powers of an equation-of-motion interaction is not generally an all-orders equivalence.
contents.limitations: The batch example proves its own finite-order scalar case and explicitly retains its induced terms; the paper's quantum Jacobian, source, and LSZ claims are not used here.

contents.name: §5.1: removing reparametrization redundancy, equations (5.1)–(5.3)
contents.support: The source shows how a perturbative local redefinition removes a leading-equation term at a chosen order and changes later orders.
contents.limitations: The physical contract records these higher-order obligations but makes no generic observable-equivalence claim; its only worked action equivalence is proved locally in the scalar example.
